scope: Crerar detailed exterior; Harper optimized exterior; Kersten, Searle, Hinds and Jones optimized exteriors; Science Quadrangle entry/walk interfaces.

crerar.standard: Detailed exterior reconstruction by source-to-model architectural correspondence, not added-frame count
source_features: Photographed recessed lower grid and massive upper cantilever
Independent limestone entry arch and glazed two-storey arrival
Connected granite landing, broad stairs and handrails
Replaced atrium/stair glazing and added smaller rooflights
limits: Mapped georeferenced footprint retained; approximate historical plan dimensions are not treated as an exact roof boundary
Local roof/eave heights, portal placement within the east frontage and individual stone-panel joints remain photographic/plan interpretations
No interior reconstruction; heraldic/lettering content not represented as readable text

photo_features: Two tall square end towers, lower stone walls and high Gothic reading-room window group
Eight central Gothic reading-room bays in the university elevation
Connected central pitched roof, attached corner turrets and stone courses
harper.limits: Hall/roof/turret sublevels and repeated openings are proportional estimates; carved sculpture is abstracted.

neighbors.U043: Kersten: different limestone Ellis Avenue and angled glazed quad fronts, pitched glazed atrium spine
neighbors.U057: Searle: four above-ground floors plus basement, flat laboratory roof and four documented heat-recovery chambers; replaces erroneous Gothic roof
neighbors.U064: Hinds: tall split-head stone service shafts and red-brick exhaust housings rise above the main flat laboratory body; six facade rows are photo-interpreted, not a published floor count
neighbors.U075: Jones: historic stone/roof/entrance character replaces generic modern academic treatment

landscape: Only short entry-to-existing-walk gap closure, existing path edges and stair clearance; no invented diagonal Quad routes; adjacent medical and Gordon geometry retained.
